Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-03
Start: 15:30 PST / 23:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Ibrahim (Redwood CSM), Priya (CTO - Kodiak), Alex (IT Ops), Samir (Platform Eng), Lena (Product), Michael (Security)

Summary: Quick kickoff to align on implementation phases, network/runbook intake, security reqs, and pilot timeline. Focus on VPC/on-prem options, data residency, and run-of-play for staging -> pilot -> canary -> prod.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll do a quick intros round, then Maya will run through the runbook intake and connectivity checklist. Ibrahim will follow on project cadence and support.
[00:12] Priya (Kodiak): Hi all, Priya here. We're excited, new project for our customer support routing using Redwood inference. Quick note: timeline is a hard quarter-goal, so we're hoping pilot in 4 weeks.
[00:24] Jordan: Got it. That's tight but doable with a focused runbook. Maya, you want to kick?
[00:28] Maya (Redwood SE): Sure, thanks. I'll call out the phases: staging connectivity, data mapping, pilot configuration (models, batch sizes, quantization profile), then go/no-go for canary. I'm going to walk the network checklist now — sorry if I stumble on some words, my internet is a bit jumpy.
[00:45] [00:45] Maya: For network we usually recommend VPC peering if you're on AWS, direct connect for higher throughput, or site-to-site VPN if you prefer. We'll need an allowlist of outbound Redwood IPs for the control plane and separate egress for inference nodes if you're using Dedicated or Private.
[01:05] Alex (Kodiak): Quick q - we are air-gapped in staging sometimes. If staging is air-gapped, can you run the pilot entirely on-prem? We don't want data leaving our network.
[01:16] Maya: Yes, we support Private deployments on-prem, though that adds lead time. For the pilot you can also use a VPC-deployed Dedicated instance with strict data residency; it avoids full on-prem procurement but keeps data in your cloud.
[01:32] Michael (Security): What's the difference in SLAs and logs between Hosted API and Private? We need immutable audit logs and KMS integration with our HSM.
[01:42] Ibrahim (Redwood CSM): Great question. For Private we provide customer-managed KMS/HSM integration options and audit log forwarding to your SIEM. SLA tiers differ — Dedicated/Private have enterprise SLAs; hosted is best-effort for lower latency but demo-friendly. We'll share the SOC2 pack and the architecture doc after the call.
[02:00] Priya: Can you quantify latency expectations? We care about <200ms p95 for short context prompts.
[02:07] Maya: For the model family you're evaluating (we recommended a distilled 7B variant), typical p95 in Dedicated setups is ~120-180ms depending on sequence length and batching. Streaming can add a small overhead, but can also improve user perceived latency. We'll include workload-shaped benchmarks.
[02:25] Samir (Platform): We're running multi-tenant microservices and would like per-route token accounting and token-level cost visibility — can your console show that?
[02:33] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level breakdowns per route and model. You can map API keys to teams and get cost by route — plus rollups for model-level spend.
[02:42] Lena (Product): For rollout, what's the most frictionless approach? Start with hosted for quick iteration then migrate?
[02:49] Maya: That's common. Many teams do hosted for early UX tests, then Dedicated for pilot to get predictable throughput and lower per-token cost. If you need private networking from day one, we can do Private but it'll add procurement steps.
[03:05] [03:05] Alex: Regarding firewall rules — what exact ports and IPs do we need to open?
[03:09] Maya: We'll provide an allowlist with CIDR blocks; control-plane uses HTTPS (443) to our endpoint and inference nodes use gRPC/HTTPS depending on runtime. We'll add specifics to the runbook note.
[03:22] Michael: For KMS — we use AWS KMS with access logs forwarded to Splunk. Can Redwood integrate with a customer KMS and not hold plaintext keys?
[03:31] Jordan: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS/HSM so Redwood never holds plaintext model encryption keys. For hosted we have managed keys but offer Bring-Your-Own-Key for enterprise tiers.
[03:44] [03:44] Priya: Ok, risks: procurement timelines and our internal security review. If Private is required, we need legal + procurement signoff.
[03:52] Ibrahim: Understood. Typical mitigation is start pilot on Dedicated in your VPC while legal for Private gets processed. That way you shrink timeline.
[04:02] Samir: One more — how does rollback/fallback work if a model regression hits prod?
[04:09] Maya: We have rollout policies in the platform: canary rollout, automatic fallback, and capacity-based routing. If a model regression is detected (via your eval hooks or our quality monitors), traffic can failover to a previous model variant or route to a lower-cost stable model. We also integrate with your tracing to flag regressions.
[04:28] [04:28] Lena: Do you provide a sample prompt suite for regression testing?
[04:31] Maya: Yes, we include a seed prompt set and recommend you augment with domain-specific prompts. We'll show the eval harness in the console.
[04:38] Alex: On networking again — any gotchas for multi-region footprint?
[04:42] Maya: Latency and data residency are the big ones. We'll propose region-based routing and cache priming. For multi-region Dedicated you can pin model versions in region and the Smart Routing layer will prefer local capacity to meet latency SLOs.
[04:57] [04:57] Jordan: Let's go through the intake checklist live — I'll read items and Alex or Michael can confirm.
[05:02] Jordan: 1) Target pilot date?
[05:04] Priya: Nov 29th would be ideal.
[05:06] Jordan: Noted. 2) Staging window for connectivity test?
[05:09] Alex: Week of Nov 8th, mornings PST.
[05:11] Jordan: 3) Do you prefer Dedicated in your AWS account or Private on-prem?
[05:15] Priya: Dedicated in AWS for pilot, Private later if needed.
[05:18] Jordan: 4) KMS requirement?
[05:19] Michael: BYOK with KMS and HSM integration, yes.
[05:23] Jordan: 5) Compliance docs requested?
[05:25] Michael: SOC2, encryption details, and penetration test summary.
[05:29] Ibrahim: We'll attach those to the CRM and share links after the call.
[05:33] [05:33] Maya: For staging we'll need an account owner who can create a short-lived role for us to deploy agents into your VPC. Alex, who would be that?
[05:41] Alex: That's me — I'll provision a role and send details.
[05:44] Maya: Great. For telemetry, do you want logs forwarded or a pull model?
[05:49] Samir: Forwarded to our Splunk instance would be ideal.
[05:53] Maya: Noted — we'll add Splunk forwarding config.
[05:57] [05:57] Jordan: Any budget constraints or procurement windows we should know?
[06:02] Priya: Budget is pre-approved for pilot; procurement window for enterprise purchase is usually 6 weeks after pilot sign-off.
[06:08] Jordan: Helpful. Competitor question — I heard you're evaluating MajorCloudAI?
[06:11] Priya: Yes, they've been in prelim talks. We like Redwood for the production observability and transparent cost levers.
[06:18] Jordan: Good to hear. Note we'll share a cost projection with different batching and quant profiles.
[06:24] [06:24] Michael: Security nit - do you support SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning?
[06:29] Maya: Yes, enterprise tiers support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. We'll ask for your SAML metadata file in a follow up.
[06:36] Jordan: Ok we're at ~40 minutes in. Ibrahim, can you summarize the timeline?
[06:40] Ibrahim: Sure — Connectivity test: week of Nov 8th. Runbook + allowlist + role details shared by Redwood: Nov 5th. Pilot kickoff (Dedicated in AWS): Nov 29th. Internal security & legal sign-off: smart to target mid-Nov for gating Private consideration. We'll have weekly check-ins until pilot completion.
[06:58] [06:58] Priya: Sounds good. One last ops question — what observability do we get during pilot for prompt-level tracing?
[07:04] Maya: You get token-level latency and cost, per-request tracing IDs, and the ability to attach evals / golden prompts for quality regression detection. We can also wire your Datadog or Splunk traces into our console.
[07:17] Jordan: Great. Let's close with explicit next steps — Maya you'll send runbook draft, Ibrahim will send SOC2 and architecture docs, Alex will share allowlist and role, Priya to confirm pilot criteria.
[07:29] Priya: Will do.
[07:31] Jordan: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the staging test and the weekly cadence.
[07:36] [07:36] Priya: Appreciate it, bye.

End of transcript.
